title: Aquí vs Acá: How to Say “Here” in Spanish
seo_title: Aquí vs Acá: How to Say “Here” in Spanish
meta_description: Aquí vs acá: both mean here, but aquí is more precise and acá vaguer and common in Latin America. Plus ahí, allí and allá, regional usage and a quiz.

body_html:
Aquí vs acá both mean “here”, and in many sentences they are interchangeable. The difference is partly meaning and partly geography. Aquí points to a more precise spot; acá is vaguer and often suggests a direction, “over here”. And while Spain uses aquí almost exclusively, in Argentina, Uruguay and much of Latin America acá is the everyday choice. Let’s also untangle the three words for “there”: ahí, allí, allá.

Quick answer
  • Aquí = here (more precise): Ponlo aquí.
  • Acá = here, over here (vaguer, direction): Ven acá.
  • Ahí = there (near the listener), allí = over there, allá = over there (vaguer, far).
  • Spain prefers aquí; Río de la Plata prefers acá; both are correct.
{{toc}}

Aquí vs acá: the core difference

AquíAcá
PrecisionA specific pointA general area or direction
ComparativesNot usually: más aquí is rareYes: más acá (closer this way)
WhereEverywhere; dominant in SpainEverywhere in Latin America; dominant in Argentina, Uruguay
ExampleFirma aquí. Sign here.Acá hace calor. It’s hot here.

The RAE’s Diccionario panhispánico de dudas notes that acá indicates a less precise location than aquí, and that in the Americas acá is often used where Spain says aquí.

When to use aquí

  • Aquí está tu café. Here’s your coffee.
  • Vivo aquí desde 2015. I’ve lived here since 2015.
  • Firme aquí, por favor. Sign here, please.
  • De aquí a mañana. Between now and tomorrow.

When to use acá

  • ¡Vení acá! Come here! (Argentina, with vos)
  • Acá en México comemos tarde. Here in Mexico we eat late.
  • Ponlo más acá. Put it a bit closer (this way).
  • De acá para allá. Back and forth, here and there.
{{image:2}}

The three “theres”: ahí, allí, allá

WordDistanceExample
ahíNear the listener, not farDéjalo ahí, en la mesa. Leave it there, on the table.
allíFar from both, specificAllí está la catedral. The cathedral is over there.
alláFar, vaguer or directionAllá en mi tierra… Back home…

The system mirrors the demonstratives: aquí/acá with este, ahí with ese, allí/allá with aquel. See {{link:este-ese-aquel|este, ese, aquel}}.

{{book:a-road-in-bloom}}

Regional notes

In Spain, acá sounds a little old-fashioned or Latin American, though it survives in phrases like de acá para allá and ven acá. In Argentina and Uruguay, acá and allá dominate and aquí sounds formal. Mexico, Colombia and much of Latin America use both, with acá very common in conversation. Whichever you choose, you’ll be understood everywhere. I cover more differences in {{link:latin-american-vs-spain-spanish|Latin American vs Spain Spanish}}.

Why this pair is tricky for learners

English has one “here” and one “there”, so having two heres and three theres feels excessive. In practice, you only need to recognize all five and actively use two or three. If you learn Spain Spanish, use aquí, ahí, allí. If you learn Argentine Spanish, use acá, ahí, allá. The real error to avoid is mixing ahí (there) with hay (there is) and ¡ay! (ouch), which sound alike: Ahí hay un hombre que dice ¡ay!

Real conversations

  • A (Madrid): ¿Dónde dejo las bolsas? (Where shall I put the bags?)
  • B: Aquí, al lado de la puerta. No, mejor ahí, junto a la silla. (Here, next to the door. No, better there, by the chair.)
  • A (Buenos Aires): ¿Hace mucho que vivís acá? (Have you lived here long?)
  • B: Diez años. Allá en Córdoba tengo a toda mi familia. (Ten years. My whole family is back in Córdoba.)

A quick mental shortcut

If you could point to the exact spot with your finger, aquí is perfect. If you mean “around here” or “this way”, acá fits better, and it is the default in the Río de la Plata. For “there”, think of the listener: next to them is ahí; far from both of you is allí, or allá if it is vague, distant or nostalgic.

One more set phrase: por aquí and por acá both mean “around here” or “this way”: ¿Hay una farmacia por aquí? (Is there a pharmacy around here?) / Por acá, por favor (This way, please).

Common mistakes

IncorrectCorrectWhy
Ahí un problema.Hay un problema.Hay = there is
AquiAquíAccent on the final í
más aquí (closer)más acáAcá accepts degrees
AllaAlláAccent on á
{{image:3}}

Try it yourself

  1. Come here! (Spain) (¡Ven aquí!)
  2. Here in Argentina we drink mate. (Acá en Argentina tomamos mate.)
  3. Leave it there, next to you. (Déjalo ahí, a tu lado.)
  4. The beach is over there. (La playa está allí.)
  5. Move it a little closer. (Ponlo un poco más acá.)

More pairs in {{link:spanish-confusing-words|my complete list of Spanish confusing words}}.

{{quiz}}

Final thoughts

Use aquí for a precise spot and acá for a general area or direction, and follow the habits of the country you’re in. Add ahí, allí and allá for “there”, and you can point to anything in Spanish.

faq.q: What is the difference between aquí and acá?
faq.a: Both mean here. Aquí refers to a more precise point, while acá is vaguer and often suggests direction. Acá is much more common in Latin America, especially Argentina and Uruguay.
Rarely, mainly in fixed phrases like de acá para allá or ven acá. Spain uses aquí almost everywhere.

faq.q: What is the difference between ahí, allí and allá?
faq.a: Ahí is there near the listener, allí is over there far from both, and allá is over there in a vaguer or more distant sense.

In Buenos Aires: ¿Vivís ___ hace mucho?
